audit_findings.title: Maintenance capital may be understated
audit_findings.magnitude: $574.8 million of 2025 net capital expenditures, equal to 96.3% of $597.1 million anchor OE; the maintenance portion and any understatement are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An insufficient maintenance-capex deduction inflates anchor OE and every projected cash flow, including terminal value, which represents 47.7%-50.9% of modeled value.
audit_findings.evidence: We regularly purchase new revenue equipment, including trucks, chassis and trailing equipment, in each of our operating segments to expand our fleets and replace aging equipment.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved methodology risk, not a demonstrated error. Its potential scale is material because JBHT is equipment-intensive and annual net capital expenditures are nearly as large as anchor OE. Even a modest sustained classification error could materially alter the modeled values.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the maintenance deduction by year to gross equipment purchases, sale and trade-in proceeds, fleet counts and ages, useful lives, replacement cycles, and identifiable expansion spending; then rerun all scenarios with the supported maintenance amount.

audit_findings.title: Insurance reserves could understate ultimate claims costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $809.7 million of claims accruals at June 30, 2026 ($322.2 million current plus $487.5 million long-term), up $54.9 million from December 31, 2025; any reserve shortfall is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adverse reserve development or an uncollectible insurance recovery would reduce future net earnings and OE; recorded claims liabilities must not also be deducted through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The ultimate cost of a claim develops over time as additional information regarding the nature, timing, and extent of damages claimed becomes available.
audit_findings.explanation: The large and rising accrual establishes meaningful exposure, but it does not demonstrate that the actuarial reserve or reimbursement assets are misstated. The filings provide no quantified shortfall, so the record cannot establish the valuation effect.
audit_findings.action: Obtain accident-year reserve-development triangles, paid-versus-incurred history, coverage-layer and aggregate limits, June 2026 insurance-recovery balances and collectability evidence; rerun OE only for a supported incremental expense or recovery impairment.

audit_findings.title: Contractor reclassification could create retroactive senior claims
audit_findings.magnitude: 2,350 independent contractors at December 31, 2025; dollar exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Reclassification could add recurring wages, benefits and payroll taxes to OE expenses and create a retroactive liability ahead of common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, such changes may be applied retroactively, and if so, we may be required to pay additional amounts to compensate individuals for prior time periods.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing describes a prospective regulatory and litigation risk but supplies no adverse determination, asserted amount, or unrecorded probable claim. It is therefore not a demonstrated current valuation adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Monitor federal and state classification changes and litigation; review contractor populations and compensation by jurisdiction and inspect subsequent filings for asserted claims or accruals before changing OE or the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Equipment-disposal losses may be double-counted
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.7 million 2025 pretax loss, equal to 2.3% of anchor OE; treating the full amount as a recurring OE add-back would increase modeled value by approximately $1.72-$2.26 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If maintenance capex is net of disposal proceeds while disposal losses remain in earnings, OE contains both the cash-sale economics and the accounting loss.
audit_findings.evidence: Net loss from sale or disposal of assets was $13.7 million in 2025, compared to a net loss from sale or disposal of assets of $14.6 million in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether double counting occurred remains unresolved, but the filed amount supplies a conservative scale ceiling. Even adding the entire pretax loss annually would move modeled values only to approximately $76.58-$100.98 per share, still far below the $273.77 valuation-date price.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE builder for gross versus net capex and the treatment of sale proceeds and disposal gains or losses; correct and rerun if net capex and an unadjusted disposal loss were both used.

audit_findings.title: Railroad concentration could invalidate the growth and terminal assumptions
audit_findings.magnitude: JBI generated $5.975 billion, or 49.8%, of 2025 revenue and $450 million, or 52.0%, of operating income; disruption downside is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adverse railroad access, service, or pricing could reduce sustainable OE growth and terminal economics, particularly in JBI.
audit_findings.evidence: While we have agreements with a number of Class I railroads, the majority of our business travels on the BNSF and the Norfolk Southern railways.
audit_findings.explanation: The concentration is demonstrated, but the supplied record shows no present termination, service collapse, or quantified adverse repricing. The possible impact is forward-looking and should be monitored rather than inserted as a current deterministic adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Track BNSF and Norfolk Southern contract duration, renewal and escalation terms, service metrics, pricing changes, volume allocation, and rerouting capacity; rerun growth and terminal assumptions if deterioration becomes evidenced.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $14.5 million FY2021 residual, computed as 2.6% of approximately $557.3 million filed D&A; $0 impact on the current $597.1 million anchor under the stated MIN(trend, latest) rule
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible residual D&A left as an expense understates historical OE and could affect the trend calculation, but the valuation anchors to the lower latest-year OE.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2021 $542.8m (97.4% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied evidence demonstrates a conservative FY2021 omission, not an overstatement. Adding the approximately $14.5 million residual to FY2021 would not raise the current anchor because the existing $658 million trend already exceeds the $597.1 million latest-year cap.
audit_findings.action: Classify the FY2021 residual from filed disclosures and document it; rerun only if eligible unidentified D&A also affects 2025 anchor OE or otherwise causes the trend to fall below the latest-year cap.
